site_name: Vantage Santa Clara second campus (CA2), Matthew/Mathew Street; permitted address 725 Matthew St, Santa Clara CA 95050
year_evidence_quote: Growing its presence in Silicon Valley, Vantage opened its first 21MW data center on its second Santa Clara campus.
year_site_match: The release describes the second Santa Clara campus as a three-building campus that will total 69MW, two miles from the flagship campus. Vantage's 2018-09-06 release calls the second campus 'our 69MW Matthew Street campus also in Santa Clara', and Data Center Frontier (2018-09-10) places it on 'a 9-acre site on Mathew Street in Santa Clara'. No page I opened names 725 Mathew St or says which building on the campus carries that number.
verification: Operator release dated January 21, 2020, headlined as a recap of 2019 ('closed out 2019 with record growth'), says the first 21MW building on the second Santa Clara campus opened. The sentence itself carries no year; 2019 comes from the release's framing, and is consistent with the two September 2018 pages that describe the Matthew Street campus as still under construction. The year is for the campus's first building, not necessarily the building at 725 Mathew St (unverified which building that is). I could not find a dated 2019 opening release; Vantage's news index only lists 2024 and later, and two guessed Vantage URLs returned 404.

lead.year_evidence_quote: Growing its presence in Silicon Valley, Vantage opened its first 21MW data center on its second Santa Clara campus.
lead.notes: Vantage's release dated 2020-01-21, a recap of 2019, says it opened the first 21 MW building on its second Santa Clara campus during that year. Vantage's 2018-09-06 release identifies the second campus as the 69 MW Matthew Street campus, which ties it to this address. No page I opened confirms that 725 is the first building rather than a later one (directories suggest 725 may be CA23). The 2019 date is for the campus's first building. Later phase years are not sourced.

site_name: QTS Denver 1 (Aurora-Denver) campus, 1160 N Gun Club Rd, Aurora CO 80018

lead.notes: QTS's own page lists 1160 N Gun Club Rd with 'Planned 160 MW+' and gives no date or status. The Colorado Sun (2023-10-11) shows the site under construction in October 2023 with a ramp to full load over 10 years. Xcel's 2024 annual report says only that it is 'working with QTS to develop' the Aurora data center. I found no non-directory page that dates the first building's operation (directories disagree, with dates from 2023 to 2026). A later Colorado Sun piece returned HTTP 429 and could not be read.

site_name: DataBank ATL4 (South Fulton), 200 Selig Dr SW, Atlanta GA 30336

lead.notes: The AJC (2023-11-01) says ATL4 is 'under construction'. DataBank's release of 2025-09-24 says the ATL4, IAD3 and LGA3 facilities 'were constructed and leased', so ATL4 was operating by September 2025. Those two dates are nearly two years apart, which is too wide to bracket the start year, and I found no DataBank opening release. DataBank's May 2022 release says the 18 acres came with 'an existing data center facility'. That older building's start year is unknown and may predate ATL4, so even 'first building at the site' is unresolved.

site_name: Microsoft Douglasville datacenter, 1601 N River Rd, Douglasville GA 30122
verification: Microsoft's fact sheet ('Published October 2025') says 'We currently are building new datacenters in Douglasville, Palmetto, and East Point, located in the vicinity of Atlanta' and 'Once operational, we expect to hire approximately 50 employees per building.' Microsoft's November 2025 economic sheet for South Fulton and Douglas counties lists only construction jobs 'Since 2019' and an 'Operational impact from 2026 – 2027'. That leans toward not yet operating, but it is inference: neither page says no Douglasville building is running, nothing ties the statement to this address, and the project has been under way since about 2021 (Rough Draft: 'the data centers in South Fulton and Douglasville moved forward'). Short of the bar for verified_not_yet_operating. No page gives an operating date either.

lead.notes: Microsoft's Georgia fact sheet, 'Published October 2025', says 'We currently are building new datacenters in Douglasville, Palmetto, and East Point'. It adds that hiring happens 'Once operational'. I am uncertain about this status: the sheet does not rule out an early building already running, and directory listings (not evidence) claim a building operating in 2024 or 2025. The 1601 N River Rd address is tied to Microsoft only by the permit and by directories. Microsoft's Fairwater Atlanta site, which began operations in October 2025, is reported to be in Fayetteville (AJC), not here.

site_name: Microsoft Palmetto datacenter, 0 Williams Road, Palmetto GA 30268
verification: The pages conflict, so neither status nor year is verified. Microsoft's October 2025 fact sheet says it is 'currently' building in Palmetto. Microsoft's undated Palmetto page (content from mid-2024) says construction 'began in April 2024 and is estimated to be complete by the beginning of October 2025'. Rough Draft Atlanta (2025-11-12) says the Fairwater Atlanta facility, 'located in South Fulton County near Palmetto, began operation in October', citing a Microsoft post; the Microsoft post I opened (2025-11-12) says only 'Atlanta' and 'began operation in October'. The AJC (2025-11-21) reports a Microsoft spokesperson placing Fairwater in Fayetteville, inside a QTS campus. If Fairwater is this site, the start year is 2025; if not, the site was still being built in October 2025. I cannot resolve which from the pages available.

lead.notes: Microsoft's October 2025 Georgia fact sheet says it is 'currently' building datacenters in Palmetto, Douglasville and East Point. Rough Draft Atlanta (2025-11-12) places the Fairwater Atlanta site, which began operating in October 2025, 'in South Fulton County near Palmetto'. The AJC (2025-11-21) instead cites a Microsoft spokesperson saying Fairwater is in Fayetteville. Because of that conflict I am uncertain about this status, and if Fairwater is actually here the site began operating in 2025. I could not tie any operating date to Williams Road.

site_name: Microsoft East Point datacenter, 4615 Ben Hill Rd, East Point GA 30349
year_evidence_quote: We currently are building new datacenters in Douglasville, Palmetto, and East Point, located in the vicinity of Atlanta.
year_site_match: Microsoft's East Point project pages describe one datacenter campus in East Point with its primary and construction entrances on Ben Hill Road ('The current construction entrance is located on Ben Hill Road just north of Somerled Trail'). They do not give the street number 4615. The fact sheet itself names only East Point.
verification: Medium, not high: the fact sheet ('Published October 2025') says Microsoft is building the East Point datacenter and speaks of operation in the future tense ('Once operational, we expect to hire approximately 50 employees per building'), but it does not say in so many words that nothing is operating. What tips it over the bar for this site is Microsoft's own East Point project pages (undated): 'The work going on now is the first phase of development, which includes one datacenter building', project phase listed as construction, project timeline 2023-2026 (that page was served in Italian; phase and timeline are my reading of it). Microsoft's November 2025 economic sheet projects 'Operational impact from 2026 – 2027'. Reading these together as 'first building not yet operating in October 2025' is inference from operator statements, not an outright statement. The same fact sheet did not clear the bar for Douglasville (no address tie, no project page) or Palmetto (conflicting news reports).

lead.notes: Microsoft's October 2025 Georgia fact sheet says 'We currently are building new datacenters in Douglasville, Palmetto, and East Point'. I found no page saying the Ben Hill Rd site is operating. I am uncertain about this status, because the sheet does not exclude a partly operating campus.

site_name: QTS Suwanee 1 DC1 (former e^deltacom data center; QTS Operations Support Center), 300 Satellite Blvd NW, Suwanee GA 30024
year_evidence_quote: In November 2000, we opened and commenced operations at an initial portion of e/\deltacom's data center in Suwanee, Georgia.
year_site_match: By a chain, not a direct address statement. ITC^DeltaCom's 10-Ks say it owned one e^deltacom data center in Suwanee. Data Center Knowledge (2009-07-14): 'In 2005 the company purchased an eDeltaCom facility in Suwanee.' QTS (2023-08-10): 'Almost 20 years ago, QTS acquired its first data center in the suburb of Suwanee, GA', home of its Operations Support Center, and says its second Suwanee building was acquired recently. QTS's Suwanee page lists 'DC1 - 300 Satellite Blvd NW' and the Operations Support Center at 300 Satellite Boulevard. No page I opened states outright that 300 Satellite was the e^deltacom building.
verification: The page supports 2000, not the claimed 2001. ITC^DeltaCom's 10-K for fiscal 2000 (filed 2001-04-02) says the first portion of the Suwanee data center opened and began operating in November 2000, about 45% of the planned space, with 'The remainder of the facility is expected to be completed in 2001.' The fiscal 2001 10-K repeats the November 2000 opening and adds 'We completed the remainder of the facility in 2001.' The fiscal 2003 10-K's 'became fully operational in 2001' (the researcher's source) therefore dates completion, not first operation. Confidence is high on the date; the tie to 300 Satellite Blvd rests on the chain described in site_match, which I judge sound but which is inference.

lead.year_evidence_quote: Our data center in Suwanee, Georgia became fully operational in 2001.
lead.notes: ITC^DeltaCom's FY2003 10-K says its Suwanee data center 'became fully operational in 2001'. Data Center Knowledge (2009) says QTS bought the eDeltaCom Suwanee facility in 2005. QTS (2023-08-10) places its first data center and Operations Support Center at 300 Satellite Boulevard. The tie between the 10-K's facility and 300 Satellite runs through that chain; the 2005 asset agreement naming 300 Satellite returned HTTP 403. Confidence is medium because 'fully operational' may postdate first operation, possibly by a year (2000).

site_name: QTS Suwanee 1 DC2 (former HP/DXC data center), 120 Satellite Blvd NW, Suwanee GA 30024

lead.notes: QTS's Suwanee page lists 'DC2 – 120 Satellite Blvd NW'. QTS's 2023-08-10 post says it 'acquired its second data center' there and that DC2 office space was being renovated. Only directories date the building's original HP-era construction (said to be 2006 to 2008) or QTS's acquisition from DXC (said to be November 2022), and I found no non-directory page giving either an original or a QTS-era start year. If the whole Suwanee 1 campus counts as one site, its first building (DC1 at 300 Satellite) dates to 2001 (see bi:541-0), but this permit is for a separate parcel and entity.

site_name: Digital Realty Lakeside Technology Center, 350 E Cermak Rd, Chicago IL 60616
verification: Neither page states when telecom or data center space first went live. Data Center Knowledge (2009-01-06): '350 East Cermak was converted to telecom use by the Carlyle Group in 1999, and owned by El Paso Global Networks from 2001-2005.' Digital Realty (2015-02-19): 'this fantastic building was purchased in 1999 and renovated for telecom use.' The owner's wording makes 1999 the purchase year with renovation following, and a purchase is not a start year under the rules. First operation in 1999 or 2000 is the plausible range (inference), but no page I opened says 'opened' or names a first tenant date. Wikipedia and Digital Realty's facility page returned 404 at the URLs I tried. If a one-year tolerance is acceptable for a site this old, 1999 is the year both pages anchor on.

lead.year_evidence_quote: 350 East Cermak was converted to telecom use by the Carlyle Group in 1999.
lead.notes: The building is a 1912 to 1929 R.R. Donnelley printing plant. Data Center Knowledge (2009-01-06) says it was converted to telecom use in 1999. Digital Realty's 2015 blog says it 'was purchased in 1999 and renovated for telecom use'. Neither page states the month the first data center or telecom space went live, so the start could fall in 1999 or 2000, and confidence is medium. Digital Realty bought it in May 2005.

site_name: Digital Realty CH1 (formerly DuPont Fabros CH1), 2200 Busse Rd, Elk Grove Village IL 60007
year_evidence_quote: DuPont Fabros' Chicago data center in Elk Grove Village, Illinois opened August 1 and is the first project it has built outside of northern Virginia
year_site_match: The 2008 article names DuPont Fabros' Chicago data center in Elk Grove Village, its only one there at the time. Data Center Knowledge (2010-11-05) calls it 'the DuPont Fabros CH1 data center in Elk Grove Village, Ill.' Area Development (2015-07-17) says CH2 opened in 2015 and 'CH2 sits across the street from CH1', so the 2008 opening can only be CH1. A tenant's facility page gives the DuPont Fabros building's address as '2200 Busse Road, Elk Grove Village, IL 60007' with 'Phase I: 2008'. The address tie comes from that tenant page, not from the 2008 article.
verification: Dated trade-press article (August 8, 2008) calls it the 'newly-opened Chicago data center' and gives the opening as August 1; the year is taken from the article date. Phase II is not verified: the tenant page lists 'Phase II: 2011', while the November 2010 Data Center Knowledge article says DuPont Fabros was still 'contemplating when to commence construction on Phase II'. The tenant page also carries a stray reference to another host's 'Chicago datacenter facility', so treat it as a weak source for anything beyond the address.

lead.year_evidence_quote: in Elk Grove Village, Illinois opened August 1 and is the first project it has built outside of northern Virginia

phases.label: Phase II (vendor page; DCK 2010 said target first half 2012)

lead.notes: Data Center Knowledge (2008-08-08) reports that DuPont Fabros' Chicago data center in Elk Grove Village opened August 1. The address tie is indirect. DuPont Fabros' second Elk Grove building (CH2, across the street) did not open until 2015, so the 2008 opening was CH1. A tenant vendor page gives CH1's address as 2200 Busse Road with 'Phase I: 2008' and 'Phase II: 2011'. The Phase II year is low confidence, since DCK in 2010 reported a target of the first half of 2012. The EPA ENERGY STAR 'Year Constructed 2011' lead likely reflects Phase II.
